issues.issue: Whether the Appeal Division unreasonably concluded that Ms. Emamifar did not make false or misleading statements or representations under subsection 52(5) of the Act.
issues.applicant_position: The Attorney General argues Ms. Emamifar's failure to report earnings was a false or misleading statement, ignoring that knowledge is not required.
issues.respondent_position: Ms. Emamifar did not make false or misleading statements; omissions are not representations under subsection 52(5).
issues.result_text: The Attorney General failed to show the Appeal Division's conclusion was unreasonable.

issues.issue: Whether the Appeal Division unreasonably applied the implied exclusion rule in interpreting subsection 52(5) to exclude omissions as false or misleading statements.
issues.applicant_position: The Attorney General argues the implied exclusion rule leads to an interpretation inconsistent with the Act's purpose, allowing improper retention of benefits.
issues.respondent_position: The Appeal Division properly applied the implied exclusion rule along with SST decisions and did not rely on it alone.
issues.result_text: The Appeal Division's reliance on implied exclusion was not improper in this case.

issues.issue: Whether the Appeal Division failed to apply the correct standard under subsection 52(5) regarding the reasonable basis for the Commission's opinion of false or misleading statements.
issues.applicant_position: The Attorney General argues the Appeal Division did not consider whether there was a reasonable basis for the Commission's opinion.
issues.respondent_position: The Appeal Division set out the appropriate standard and implicitly found no reasonable basis for the Commission's opinion.
issues.result_text: The Appeal Division's findings imply no reasonable basis for the Commission's opinion.
